extra.message: The /api/search endpoint reflects user-controlled req.query.searchTerm directly into the response body via res.send(). Express res.send() with a string sets Content-Type to text/html, so arbitrary HTML/JavaScript supplied in the searchTerm query parameter is echoed back unencoded. The Angular client then renders this value with $sce.trustAsHtml() and ng-bind-html (xss-search.controller.js:35 and xss-search.html:18), resulting in reflected cross-site scripting.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The server response (which reflects the attacker-controlled search term) is explicitly marked as trusted HTML via $sce.trustAsHtml() and then rendered through ng-bind-html in xss-search.html:18. This deliberately disables Angular's sanitization for user-controlled input, enabling reflected XSS.

Since the profile is writable by an unauthenticated attacker (see CSRF finding) with arbitrary HTML/JavaScript, this is stored cross-site scripting.

extra.message: getProfile (lines 32-36) and updateProfile (lines 38-49) perform no server-side authentication or authorization. The value of the client-controlled cookie req.cookies.userAuthToken is used directly as the key into the in-memory data.profile object. Any user can read or overwrite any profile by simply setting their userAuthToken cookie to an arbitrary value (e.g., '35592211433686316'), enabling broken access control and insecure direct object reference (IDOR).

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The profile key is taken directly from the userAuthToken cookie (user = req.cookies.userAuthToken) and assigned data.profile[user] = req.body. Because data.profile is a plain object, a cookie value of '__proto__' (or 'constructor'/'prototype') will assign to the object's prototype, allowing an attacker to pollute Object.prototype with attacker-controlled JSON (prototype pollution, CWE-1321).

cwe: CWE-1321: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')

extra.message: The login handler discards the random session value and hardcodes the auth token to the fixed string '35592211433686316' (the Math.random() result is overwritten). The session token is therefore predictable and hardcoded, allowing any attacker to forge a valid session cookie without ever logging in.

The POST /api/user/profile endpoint (updateProfile) relies solely on a cookie (userAuthToken) for session identity and performs no CSRF-token validation, no SameSite cookie attribute, and no origin/Referer check. A cross-site form or request (as demonstrated by attacker-app/src/client/app/csrf-attack/csrf-attack.html) can silently change a victim's profile because the browser automatically sends the session cookie.

The userAuthToken session cookie is set without the httpOnly flag (and without the secure or SameSite flags). Given the presence of reflected and stored XSS elsewhere in the app, JavaScript running in the victim's browser can read document.cookie and exfiltrate the session token, enabling session hijacking.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: The application does not send an X-Frame-Options header or a Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors directive; the CSP middleware and the 'x-powered-by' disabling are commented out. This allows the application to be framed by attacker pages, enabling clickjacking (as demonstrated by attacker-app/src/client/app/clickjacking-attack/clickjacking-attack.html).

cwe: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames

extra.message: Sensitive data is written to server logs: the userAuthToken session token (line 33), the profile contents (line 34), and the full request body (lines 40-42) are logged with console.log. This leaks session tokens and personal data to anyone with access to the logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
